messages:
samira: Announcement: next week were enabling a 'Telemetry Safe Mode' and a customer-controlled 'Retention Lock' for Private/VPC deployments. Intent: give regulated customers finer control over whether telemetry can be included in on-prem exports and how long exported artifacts remain accessible. Opt-in and contract-driven.

samira: Short bullets: 
- Telemetry Safe Mode: defaults telemetry-off for all exports and snapshots. Customers can opt into specific telemetry classes (e.g., perf, metrics, debug) via a signed addendum.
- Retention Lock: tenants can request an export artifact retention window (7/30/90 days) or set a contract-level permanent retention lock if their legal team requires it.
- Agent requirement: v3.2+ with safe-mode flag enabled.

igor: Ops impact: will add per-tenant retention metadata and an enforced lifecycle job to purge artifacts after retention window. Also adding a console control to set retention and to lock it (legal confirmation required). Canary Tue -> broad Wed.

legal: Legal note: any change to retention beyond default must be captured in a signed amendment. Permanent retention locks require a countersigned contract and an audit field recording approver identity. Draft templates uploaded to /legal/templates/retention-lock-amendment.md.

natalie: Security: Telemetry Safe Mode means we will never include telemetry in exports unless the addendum explicitly lists allowed types. If telemetry is allowed, exports will still be encrypted and HSM-signed and telemetry included will be minimal and enumerated. We'll publish the allowed-telemetry matrix in docs.

ops-bot: deploy-schedule: safe-mode + retention controls canary 2026-08-03T09:00Z -> 2026-08-03T11:00Z. Auto-rollback on threshold.

samira: Customer UX example (console):
1) Tenant admin toggles "Enable Telemetry Exports" -> modal shows required addendum link and checkbox to confirm admin identity.
2) Tenant selects retention window (7/30/90 or request permanent lock).
3) If permanent lock requested, display warning and require uploaded signed amendment.

samira: API example (requesting telemetry-on and 30d retention):
```bash
curl -X POST "https://private-console.redwood.example/api/v1/tenants/TENANT/settings/export_prefs" \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"telemetry_enabled":true,"telemetry_types":["perf"],"retention_days":30,"signed_addendum":"BASE64_PDF"}'
```

igor: Ops action items: implement enforcement job to purge expired artifacts, add console lock UX, and add alerts for retention policy violations. Also add migration to annotate existing artifacts with retention metadata.

natalie: Sec action items: define telemetry classes and minimum redaction when telemetry is included; publish verification steps for exported artifacts; ensure HSM signing covers retention metadata.

legal: Action items: finalize retention-lock amendment and addendum templates; document required evidence for permanent locks; provide CS with a checklist for signed consents.

samira: SLAs: Nothing changes for inference. Exports remain background best-effort. Retention enforcement is internal and best-effort on purge timing, but well aim to purge within 24h of expiration. Permanent locks are irreversible without legal reversal paperwork.

sec-eng: One question: for permanent locks, do we keep a signed timestamped ledger of the lock that customers and auditors can verify?

legal: Yes  we'll include a signed ledger entry (manifest) with each retention-lock request and include the signer identity and timestamp; entry will be HSM-signed.

samira: Please ack and tag if you need demo tenant access. We'll run two rehearsals with Legal/CS next week. :lock:
